questions.text: Write about the Dalit movement.
questions.text_as_printed: Write about the Dalit movement. (Average )

answer.value: Dalits had no place in the caste system; they were socially excluded from the mainstream of society due to being born in untouchable castes with no social status. Many struggles were waged against this. The original inspiration for Dalits was Dr. B. R. Ambedkar's ideological stances; education, organization and struggles were the seed mantras of Dalit movements. In the Hyderabad Karnataka region, B. Shamsundara founded the BhimaSena organization in 1970. He gave a new twist to the Dalit movement. Following the Basavalingappa Boosa case, the Karnataka Dalit SangharshSamiti was established and this committee fought for the Dalits.

questions.text: Achievements of the Dalit Movement
questions.text_as_printed: Achievements of the Dalit Movement (Difficult )

answer.value: Achievements of the Dalit Movement: In 1936, under the leadership of M. C. Rajah, a prominent Dalit leader of South India, Dalits were allowed to enter the Mysore Palace. Education, organisation, and struggle became the guiding principles of the Dalit Movement. Dalits became politically and socially organised to solve their community's problems. Dr. B. R. Ambedkar became a symbol of self-respect and earned the title "Dalit Surya" (Sun of the Dalits). The Basavalingappa Boosa controversy became a turning point. Traditionally landless Dalits began movements demanding land rights. Another major objective was educational progress and access to positions of power and administration. Today, Dalits play a significant role in all spheres of society.
